summary: Gaston Paris (1839–1903) was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez (circa 1858–1860) and at the École des chartes (circa 1858–1862). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1868–1895) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau (1879–1967) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique circa 1899–1901.

Gaton Ngawang Lekpa (1864–1941) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and later taught Shenphen Nangwa and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima.

Gauri Viswanathan (b. 1950) studied at the University of Delhi (circa 1968–1973) and Columbia University (circa 1980–1985). She taught English at Delhi (circa 1973–1978) and became Professor in the Humanities and South Asia Institute Director at Columbia (circa 1989).

Gaurinath Sastri (1909–1995) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (circa 1957–1969), Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1959), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (circa 1970–1978).

Gavin D'Costa (b. 1958) studied at Cambridge (circa 1980–1982) and Birmingham (circa 1982–1985). Working in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at West London Institute (circa 1985–1993) and held a post at the University of Bristol beginning in 1993.

Gavin Flood (b. 1954) studied at Lancaster University (circa 1976–1988). Active in Indology and religious studies, he held posts at Lampeter (circa 1991–2003), Stirling (circa 2003–2005), the University of Oxford (2005–2015), and Yale-NUS College (2016).
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indology doctoral student and faculty member at the University of Tübingen, studying under Claire Maes (attested 2026).

Gelek is a Tibetology scholar who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998). He has also held appointments as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rimpoche (1939–2017) studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School (circa 1960–1963), and Cornell (1964). In Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he directed Tibet House in New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving instruction from traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki (1935–2015) studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1955–1959, doctorate 1991). Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, he was a researcher at Toyo Bunko (circa 1966–1977) and professor at Kokugakuin University (2006).

Gendun Chopel (1903–1951) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Drisha, Labrang (1920), Kumbum (circa 1920–1927), and Drepung (1927) monasteries, and under Sherab Gyatso (1927) and Gendun Tendzin Gyatso.

Gendun Chophel (1903–1952) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso circa 1921–1927. He held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941 and taught Horkhang Sonam Palbar.

Gendun Rinpoche (1918–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He served as abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling from circa 1977 to 1997, and founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, Dhagpo Dargye Ling, and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling.

Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) studied at Kyoto University. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Hamburg (1956), Otani University (attested 1974–1976 and 1987–1995), Harvard University, and Osaka University (attested 1995).
Genro (1717–1789) was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of first seat (第一座) at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima (1912–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1931 to 1934. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1957 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) studied at Waseda University (circa 1945–1951, PhD 1983). Working in Japanology and Buddhist studies, he served as assistant professor at Kokushikan University (circa 1965–1970) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).
Genshu Watanabe (1869–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and trained under Sogaku Harada as a dharma heir.
